note: Threat cards are SoCHarness summaries in its own words. Technique ids are MITRE ATLAS or OWASP; tests point at checks that exist in SoCHarness today.

cards.title: Direct prompt injection and jailbreaks
cards.what: A user types instructions meant to override the system prompt or talk the model out of its rules, sometimes obfuscated to slip past filters.
preconditions: People can type to the model
The model holds rules or data the user should not reach

cards.title: Indirect prompt injection
cards.what: Instructions hidden in content the model reads (email, documents, web pages, tool output, logs) redirect what it does, without the user typing anything.
preconditions: The model reads content an outsider can write
The model can act or answer on that content

tests.label: Test ground TG-10: log text that tries to give the agent orders
AgentDojo: injected tool output against utility and security

cards.title: System prompt and configuration extraction
cards.what: Users coax the model into revealing its instructions, tool definitions or embedded secrets, which then guide further attacks.
preconditions: A system prompt or tool definitions exist
Secrets or business rules are written into them

cards.title: Retrieval (RAG) poisoning
cards.what: Content planted where a retrieval index will pick it up steers answers or carries injected instructions to every user who triggers it.
preconditions: Answers draw on an index or search results
Someone outside the owning team can add or edit indexed content

cards.title: Memory and context poisoning
cards.what: A malicious entry saved into agent memory or shared context keeps influencing decisions in later sessions.
preconditions: The agent writes to persistent memory or shared context
Later sessions read it back

cards.title: Tool misuse and excessive agency
cards.what: The agent is steered into calling tools it legitimately holds in harmful ways: changing or deleting data, chaining calls, or acting beyond the task.
preconditions: The agent can call tools that change things
Some of those calls need no human approval

tests.label: AgentDojo: injected tool output against utility and security

cards.title: Data exfiltration through agent tools and output
cards.what: Sensitive data the agent can see is sent out through a tool (email, HTTP, tickets) or leaks into an answer.
preconditions: The agent sees confidential or restricted data
A tool or channel can carry data outside

tests.label: AgentDojo: injected tool output against utility and security

cards.title: Poisoned or swapped tools and MCP servers
cards.what: A third-party tool, plugin or MCP server ships malicious descriptions or changes behaviour after it has been approved (a "rug pull").
preconditions: Agents load tools or MCP servers you did not write
Tool descriptions are trusted as instructions

cards.title: Model and framework supply chain
cards.what: A model, adapter, dataset or framework package from outside is tampered with, vulnerable or silently replaced.
preconditions: You run third-party models, open weights or AI frameworks

cards.title: Training and fine-tuning data poisoning
cards.what: Whoever can influence training or fine-tuning data plants a backdoor or bias that later decisions inherit.
preconditions: You train or fine-tune models
Training data includes sources others can influence

cards.title: Model extraction and theft
cards.what: Repeated queries copy a model's behaviour, or weights and artefacts are stolen outright.
preconditions: The model can be queried at volume
The model or its outputs have commercial value

cards.title: Adversarial evasion of predictive models
cards.what: Inputs are shaped so a classifier or scoring model (fraud, malware, spam) makes the wrong call while looking normal.
preconditions: A predictive model makes or gates decisions
Attackers can probe it and see the outcome

cards.title: Unsafe output handling and rendering
cards.what: Model output is rendered or passed on without checks, so links, images, markup or commands in it reach people and systems.
preconditions: Output is shown in a browser, email or UI, or fed to another system

cards.title: Unexpected code execution
cards.what: Generated or injected code runs in the agent's environment, CI or connected systems without the intended review.
preconditions: The agent can run code, shell commands or tests

cards.title: Agent identity and privilege abuse
cards.what: Credentials, tokens or delegated roles held by the agent or its tools are harvested or used beyond what the user may do.
preconditions: The agent holds credentials or can change access

cards.title: Manipulated human approvals
cards.what: A convincing but wrong explanation from the agent gets a risky action approved by a person who trusts it.
preconditions: Risky actions wait for human approval
Approvers rely on the agent's own summary

cards.title: Inter-agent manipulation and cascading failures
cards.what: Messages between agents are spoofed or poisoned, and one bad step spreads through connected agents faster than people can stop it.
preconditions: Agents pass work or messages to other agents

cards.title: Denial of service and cost harvesting
cards.what: Floods of requests or deliberately expensive prompts exhaust capacity or run up model spend.
preconditions: Outsiders can reach the application or its API

cards.title: Confident, unsupported answers
cards.what: The model states things its evidence does not support and people act on them; attackers can also exploit predictable hallucinations.
preconditions: People act on the answers
Answers are not checked against sources

tests.label: Test-ground grading flags unsupported claims (grounding guard)
